verses.zh: 耶和华说：祸哉！这悖逆的儿女。他们同谋，却不由于我，结盟，却不由于我的灵，以致罪上加罪；
verses.en: “The rebellious[NOTE:1] children are as good as dead,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord,“those who make plans without consulting me,[NOTE:3] who form alliances without consulting my Spirit,[NOTE:4] and thereby compound their sin.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “stubborn” (NCV); cf. NIV “obstinate.”
Heb “Woe [to] rebellious children.”
Heb “making a plan, but not from me.”

Heb “and pouring out a libation, but not [from] my spirit.” This translation assumes that the verb נָסַךְ (nasakh) means “pour out,” and that the cognate noun מַסֵּכָה (massekhah) means “libation.” In this case “pouring out a libation” alludes to a ceremony that formally ratifies an alliance. Another option is to understand the verb נָסַךְ as a homonym meaning “weave,” and the cognate noun מַסֵּכָה as a homonym meaning “covering.” In this case forming an alliance is likened to weaving a garment.
Heb “consequently adding sin to sin.”

verses.zh: 起身下埃及去，并没有求问我；要靠法老的力量加添自己的力量，并投在埃及的荫下。
verses.en: They travel down to Egyptwithout seeking my will,[NOTE:1] seeking Pharaoh’s protection,and looking for safety in Egypt’s protective shade.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “those who go to descend to Egypt, but [of] my mouth they do not inquire.”
Heb “to seek protection in the protection of Pharaoh, and to seek refuge in the shade of Egypt.”

verses.zh: 所以，法老的力量必作你们的羞辱；投在埃及的荫下，要为你们的惭愧。
verses.en: But Pharaoh’s protection will bring you nothing but shameand the safety of Egypt’s protective shade nothing but humiliation.

verses.zh: 他们的首领已在琐安；他们的使臣到了哈内斯。
verses.en: Though his[NOTE:1] officials are in Zoanand his messengers arrive at Hanes,[NOTE:2]
notes: This probably refers to Judah’s officials and messengers.
Zoan was located in the Egyptian delta in the north; Hanes was located somewhere in southern region of lower Egypt, south of Memphis; the exact location is debated.

verses.zh: 他们必因那不利于他们的民蒙羞。那民并非帮助，也非利益，只作羞耻凌辱。
verses.en: all will be put to shame[NOTE:1] because of a nation that cannot help them,who cannot give them aid or help,but only shame and disgrace.”
notes: The present translation follows the marginal (Qere) reading of the Hebrew text; the consonantal text (Kethib) has “made to stink, decay.”

verses.zh: 论南方牲畜的默示：他们把财物驮在驴驹的脊背上，将宝物驮在骆驼的肉鞍上，经过艰难困苦之地，就是公狮、母狮、蝮蛇、火焰的飞龙之地，往那不利于他们的民那里去。
verses.en: This is an oracle[NOTE:1] about the animals in the Negev:Through a land of distress and danger,inhabited by lionesses and roaring lions,[NOTE:2] by snakes and darting adders,[NOTE:3] they transport their wealth on the backs of donkeys,their riches on the humps of camels,to a nation that cannot help them.[NOTE:4]
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.

Heb “[a land of] a lioness and a lion, from them.” Some emend מֵהֶם (mehem, “from them”) to מֵהֵם (mehem), an otherwise unattested Hiphil participle from הָמַם (hamam, “move noisily”). Perhaps it would be better to take the initial mem (מ) as enclitic and emend the form to הֹמֶה (homeh), a Qal active participle from הָמָה (hamah, “to make a noise”); cf. J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:542, n. 9.
Heb “flying burning ones.” See the note at 14:29.
This verse describes messengers from Judah transporting wealth to Egypt in order to buy Pharaoh’s protection through a treaty.

verses.zh: 埃及的帮助是徒然无益的；所以我称她为「坐而不动的拉哈伯」。
verses.en: Egypt is totally incapable of helping.[NOTE:1] For this reason I call her“Proud one[NOTE:2] who is silenced.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “As for Egypt, with vanity and emptiness they help.”

Heb “Rahab” (רַהַב, rahav), which also appears as a name for Egypt in Ps 87:4. The epithet is also used in the OT for a mythical sea monster symbolic of chaos. See the note at 51:9. A number of English versions use the name “Rahab” (e.g., ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV) while others attempt some sort of translation (cf. CEV “a helpless monster”; TEV, NLT “the Harmless Dragon”).

The MT reads “Rahab, they, sitting.” The translation above assumes an emendation of הֵם שָׁבֶת (hem shavet) to הַמָּשְׁבָּת (hammashbat), a Hophal participle with prefixed definite article, meaning “the one who is made to cease,” i.e., “destroyed,” or “silenced.” See HALOT 444-45 s.v. ישׁב.

verses.zh: 现今你去，在他们面前将这话刻在版上，写在书上，以便传留后世，直到永永远远。
verses.en: Now go, write it[NOTE:1] down on a tablet in their presence;[NOTE:2] inscribe it on a scrollso that it might be preserved for a future timeas an enduring witness.[NOTE:3]
notes: The referent of the third feminine singular pronominal suffix is uncertain. Perhaps it refers to the preceding message, which accuses the people of rejecting the Lord’s help in favor of an alliance with Egypt.
Heb “with them.” On the use of the preposition here, see BDB 86 s.v. II אֵת.

Recording the message will enable the prophet to use it in the future as evidence that God warned his people of impending judgment and clearly spelled out the nation’s guilt. An official record of the message will also serve as proof of the prophet’s authority as God’s spokesman.

verses.zh: 因为他们是悖逆的百姓、说谎的儿女，不肯听从耶和华训诲的儿女。
verses.en: For these are rebellious people—they are lying children,children unwilling to obey the Lord’s law.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or perhaps, “instruction” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV); NCV, TEV “teachings.”

verses.zh: 他们对先见说：不要望见不吉利的事，对先知说：不要向我们讲正直的话；要向我们说柔和的话，言虚幻的事。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] say to the visionaries, “See no more visions!”and to the seers, “Don’t relate messages to us about what is right![NOTE:2] Tell us nice things;relate deceptive messages.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “who” (so NASB, NRSV). A new sentence was started here in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “Do not see for us right things.”
Heb “Tell us smooth things, see deceptive things.”

verses.zh: 你们要离弃正道，偏离直路，不要在我们面前再提说以色列的圣者。
verses.en: Turn aside from the way;stray off the path.[NOTE:1] Remove from our presence the Holy One of Israel.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The imagery refers to the way or path of truth, as revealed by God to the prophet.
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

verses.zh: 所以，以色列的圣者如此说：因为你们藐视这训诲的话，倚赖欺压和乖僻，以此为可靠的，
verses.en: For this reason this is what the Holy One of Israel says:“You have rejected this message;[NOTE:1] you trust instead in your ability to oppress and trick,[NOTE:2] and rely on that kind of behavior.[NOTE:3]
notes: The sentence actually begins with the word “because.” In the Hebrew text vv. 12-13 are one long sentence.
Heb “and you trust in oppression and cunning.”
Heb “and you lean on it”; NAB “and depend on it.”

verses.zh: 故此，这罪孽在你们身上，好像将要破裂凸出来的高墙，顷刻之间忽然坍塌；
verses.en: So this sin will become your downfall.You will be like a high wall that bulges and cracks and is ready to collapse;it crumbles suddenly, in a flash.[NOTE:1]
notes: The verse reads literally, “So this sin will become for you like a breach ready to fall, bulging on a high wall, the breaking of which comes suddenly, in a flash.” Their sin produces guilt and will result in judgment. Like a wall that collapses their fall will be swift and sudden.

verses.zh: 要被打碎，好像把窑匠的瓦器打碎，毫不顾惜，甚至碎块中找不到一片可用以从炉内取火，从池中舀水。
verses.en: It shatters in pieces like a clay jar,so shattered to bits that none of it can be salvaged.[NOTE:1] Among its fragments one cannot find a shard large enough[NOTE:2] to scoop a hot coal from a fire[NOTE:3] or to skim off water from a cistern.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Its shattering is like the shattering of a jug of [i.e., “made by”] potters, [so] shattered one cannot save [any of it].”
The words “large enough” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “to remove fire from the place of kindling.”
On the meaning of גֶבֶא (geveh, “cistern”) see HALOT 170 s.v.

verses.zh: 主耶和华―以色列的圣者曾如此说：你们得救在乎归回安息；你们得力在乎平静安稳；你们竟自不肯。
verses.en: For this is what the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One of Israel says:“If you repented and patiently waited for me, you would be delivered;[NOTE:1] if you calmly trusted in me, you would find strength,[NOTE:2] but you are unwilling.
notes: Heb “in returning and in quietness you will be delivered.” Many English versions render the last phrase “shall be saved” or something similar (e.g., NAB, NASB, NRSV).
Heb “in quietness and in trust is your strength” (NASB and NRSV both similar).

verses.zh: 你们却说：不然，我们要骑马奔走。所以你们必然奔走；又说：我们要骑飞快的牲口。所以追赶你们的，也必飞快。
verses.en: You say, ‘No, we will flee on horses,’so you will indeed flee.You say, ‘We will ride on fast horses,’so your pursuers will be fast.

verses.zh: 一人叱喝，必令千人逃跑；五人叱喝，你们都必逃跑；以致剩下的，好像山顶的旗杆，冈上的大旗。
verses.en: One thousand will scurry at the battle cry of one enemy soldier;[NOTE:1] at the battle cry of five enemy soldiers you will all run away,[NOTE:2] until the remaining few are as isolated[NOTE:3] as a flagpole on a mountaintopor a signal flag on a hill.”
notes: Heb “One thousand from before [or “because of”] one battle cry.” גְּעָרָה (geʿarah) is often defined as “threat,” but in war contexts it likely refers to a shout or battle cry. See Ps 76:6.
Heb “from before [or “because of”] the battle cry of five you will flee.
Heb “until you are left” (so NAB, NASB, NRSV).

verses.zh: 耶和华必然等候，要施恩给你们；必然兴起，好怜悯你们。因为耶和华是公平的　神；凡等候他的都是有福的！
verses.en: For this reason the Lord is ready to show you mercy;he sits on his throne, ready to have compassion on you.[NOTE:1] Indeed, the Lord is a just God;all who wait for him in faith will be blessed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Therefore the Lord waits to show you mercy, and therefore he is exalted to have compassion on you.” The logical connection between this verse and what precedes is problematic. The point seems to be that Judah’s impending doom does not bring God joy. Rather the prospect of their suffering stirs within him a willingness to show mercy and compassion, if they are willing to seek him on his terms.
Heb “Blessed are all who wait for him.”

verses.zh: 百姓必在锡安、在耶路撒冷居住；你不再哭泣。主必因你哀求的声音施恩给你；他听见的时候就必应允你。
verses.en: For people will live in Zion;in Jerusalem[NOTE:1] you will weep no more.[NOTE:2] When he hears your cry of despair, he will indeed show you mercy;when he hears it, he will respond to you.[NOTE:3]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

Heb “For people in Zion will live; in Jerusalem, you will weep no more.” The phrase “in Jerusalem” could be taken with what precedes. Some prefer to emend יֵשֵׁב (yeshev, “will live,” a Qal imperfect) to יֹשֵׁב (yoshev, a Qal active participle) and translate “For [you] people in Zion, who live in Jerusalem, you will weep no more.”
Heb “he will indeed show you mercy at the sound of your crying out; when he hears, he will answer you.”

verses.zh: 主虽然以艰难给你当饼，以困苦给你当水，你的教师却不再隐藏；你眼必看见你的教师。
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] will give you distress to eatand suffering to drink;[NOTE:2] but your teachers will no longer be hidden;your eyes will see them.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
Heb “and the Master will give to you bread—distress, and water—oppression.”

Heb “but your teachers will no longer be hidden; your eyes will be seeing your teachers.” The translation assumes that the form מוֹרֶיךָ (morekha) is a plural participle, referring to spiritual leaders such as prophets and priests. Another possibility is that the form is actually singular (see GKC 273-74 §93.ss) or a plural of respect, referring to God as the master teacher. See HALOT 560-61 s.v. III מוֹרֶה. For discussion of the views, see J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:560.

verses.zh: 你或向左或向右，你必听见后边有声音说：「这是正路，要行在其间。」
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] will hear a word spoken behind you, saying,“This is the correct[NOTE:2] way, walk in it,”whether you are heading to the right or the left.
notes: Heb “your ears” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
The word “correct’ is supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 你雕刻偶像所包的银子和铸造偶像所镀的金子，你要玷污，要抛弃，好像污秽之物，对偶像说：「去吧！」
verses.en: You will desecrate your silver-plated idols[NOTE:1] and your gold-plated images.[NOTE:2] You will throw them away as if they were a menstrual rag,saying to them, “Get out!”
notes: Heb “the platings of your silver idols.”
Heb “the covering of your gold image.”

verses.zh: 你将种子撒在地里，主必降雨在其上，并使地所出的粮肥美丰盛。到那时，你的牲畜必在宽阔的草场吃草。
verses.en: He will water the seed you plant in the ground,and the ground will produce crops in abundance.[NOTE:1] At that time[NOTE:2] your cattle will graze in wide pastures.
notes: Heb “and he will give rain for your seed that you plant in the ground, and food [will be] the produce of the ground, and it will be rich and abundant.”
Or “in that day” (KJV).

verses.zh: 耕地的牛和驴驹必吃加盐的料；这料是用木杴和杈子扬净的。
verses.en: The oxen and donkeys used in plowing[NOTE:1] will eat seasoned feed winnowed with a shovel and pitchfork.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the oxen and the donkeys that work the ground.”
Crops will be so abundant that even the work animals will eat well.

verses.zh: 在大行杀戮的日子，高台倒塌的时候，各高山冈陵必有川流河涌。
verses.en: On every high mountainand every high hillthere will be streams flowing with water,at the time of[NOTE:1] great slaughter when the fortified towers collapse.
notes: Or “in the day of” (KJV).

verses.zh: 当耶和华缠裹他百姓的损处，医治他民鞭伤的日子，月光必像日光，日光必加七倍，像七日的光一样。
verses.en: The light of the full moon will be like the sun’s glare,and the sun’s glare will be seven times brighter,like the light of seven days,[NOTE:1] when the Lord binds up his people’s fractured bones[NOTE:2] and heals their severe wound.[NOTE:3]
notes: Light here symbolizes restoration of divine blessing and prosperity. The number “seven” is used symbolically to indicate intensity. The exact meaning of the phrase “the light of seven days” is uncertain; it probably means “seven times brighter” (see the parallel line).
Heb “the fracture of his people” (so NASB). sn The Lord is here compared to a physician setting a broken bone in a bandage or cast.

Heb “the injury of his wound.” The joining of synonyms emphasizes the severity of the wound. Another option is to translate, “the wound of his blow.” In this case the pronominal suffix might refer to the Lord, not the people, yielding the translation, “the wound which he inflicted.”

verses.zh: 看哪，耶和华的名从远方来，怒气烧起，密烟上腾。他的嘴唇满有忿恨；他的舌头像吞灭的火。
verses.en: Look, the name[NOTE:1] of the Lord comes from a distant placein raging anger and awesome splendor.[NOTE:2] He speaks angrily,and his word is like destructive fire.[NOTE:3]
notes: The “name” of the Lord sometimes stands by metonymy for the Lord himself, see Exod 23:21; Lev 24:11; Pss 54:1 (54:3 HT); 124:8. In Isa 30:27 the point is that he reveals that aspect of his character which his name suggests—he comes as Yahweh (“he is present”), the ever present helper of his people who annihilates their enemies and delivers them. The name “Yahweh” originated in a context where God assured a fearful Moses that he would be with him as he confronted Pharaoh and delivered Israel from slavery in Egypt. See Exod 3.

Heb “his anger burns, and heaviness of elevation.” The meaning of the phrase “heaviness of elevation” is unclear, for מַשָּׂאָה (massaʾah, “elevation”) occurs only here. Some understand the term as referring to a cloud (elevated above the earth’s surface), in which case one might translate, “and in heavy clouds” (cf. NAB “with lowering clouds”). Others relate the noun to מָשָׂא (masaʾ, “burden”) and interpret it as a reference to judgment. In this case one might translate, “and with severe judgment.” The present translation assumes that the noun refers to his glory and that “heaviness” emphasizes its degree.
Heb “his lips are full of anger, and his tongue is like consuming fire.” The Lord’s lips and tongue are used metonymically for his word (or perhaps his battle cry; see v. 31).

verses.zh: 他的气如涨溢的河水，直涨到颈项，要用毁灭的筛箩筛净列国，并且在众民的口中必有使人错行的嚼环。
verses.en: His battle cry overwhelms like a flooding river[NOTE:1] that reaches one’s neck.He shakes the nations in a sieve that isolates the chaff;[NOTE:2] he puts a bit into the mouth of the nations and leads them to destruction.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his breath is like a flooding river.” This might picture the Lord breathing heavily as he runs down his enemy, but in light of the preceding verse, which mentions his lips and tongue, “breath” probably stands metonymically for the word or battle cry that he expels from his mouth as he shouts. In Isa 34:16 and Ps 33:6 the Lord’s “breath” is associated with his command.

Heb “shaking nations in a sieve of worthlessness.” It is not certain exactly how שָׁוְא (shaveʾ, “emptiness, worthlessness”) modifies “sieve.” A sieve is used to separate grain from chaff and isolate what is worthless so that it might be discarded. Perhaps the nations are likened to such chaff; God’s judgment will sift them out for destruction.

Heb “and a bit that leads astray [is] in the jaws of the peoples.” Here the nations are likened to a horse that can be controlled by a bit placed in its mouth. In this case the Lord uses his sovereign control over the “horse” to lead it to its demise.

verses.zh: 你们必唱歌，像守圣节的夜间一样，并且心中喜乐，像人吹笛，上耶和华的山，到以色列的磐石那里。
verses.en: You will singas you do in the evening when you are celebrating a festival.You will be happy like one who plays a fluteas he goes to the mountain of the Lord, the Rock who shelters Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “[you will have] joy of heart, like the one going with a flute to enter the mountain of the Lord to the Rock of Israel.” The image here is not a foundational rock, but a rocky cliff where people could hide for protection (for example, the fortress of Masada).

verses.zh: 耶和华必使人听他威严的声音，又显他降罚的膀臂和他怒中的忿恨，并吞灭的火焰与霹雷、暴风、冰雹。
verses.en: The Lord will give a mighty shout[NOTE:1] and intervene in power,[NOTE:2] with furious anger and flaming, destructive fire,[NOTE:3] with a driving rainstorm and hailstones.
notes: Heb “the Lord will cause the splendor of his voice to be heard.”
Heb “and reveal the lowering of his arm.”
Heb “and a flame of consuming fire.”

verses.zh: 亚述人必因耶和华的声音惊惶；耶和华必用杖击打他。
verses.en: Indeed, the Lord’s shout will shatter Assyria;[NOTE:1] he will beat them with a club.
notes: Heb “Indeed by the voice of the Lord Assyria will be shattered.”

verses.zh: 耶和华必将命定的杖加在他身上；每打一下，人必击鼓弹琴。打仗的时候，耶和华必抡起手来，与他交战。
verses.en: Every blow from his punishing cudgel[NOTE:1] with which the Lord will beat them[NOTE:2] will be accompanied by music from the[NOTE:3] tambourine and harp,and he will attack them with his weapons.[NOTE:4]
notes: The Hebrew text has “every blow from a founded [i.e., “appointed”?] cudgel.” The translation above, with support from a few medieval Hebrew mss, assumes an emendation of מוּסָדָה (musadah, “founded”) to מוּסָרֹה (musaroh, “his discipline”).
Heb “which the Lord lays on him.”
Heb “will be with” (KJV similar).

The Hebrew text reads literally, “and with battles of brandishing [weapons?] he will fight against him.” Some prefer to emend וּבְמִלְחֲמוֹת (uvemilkhamot, “and with battles of”) to וּבִמְחֹלוֹת (uvimkholot, “and with dancing”). Note the immediately preceding references to musical instruments.

verses.zh: 原来陀斐特又深又宽，早已为王预备好了；其中堆的是火与许多木柴。耶和华的气如一股硫磺火使他着起来。
verses.en: For[NOTE:1] the burial place is already prepared;[NOTE:2] it has been made deep and wide for the king.[NOTE:3] The firewood is piled high on it.[NOTE:4] The Lord’s breath, like a stream flowing with brimstone,will ignite it.
notes: Or “indeed.”

The Hebrew text reads literally, “for arranged from before [or “yesterday”] is [?].” The meaning of תָּפְתֶּה (tofteh), which occurs only here, is unknown. The translation above (as with most English versions) assumes an emendation to תֹּפֶת (tofet, “Topheth”; cf. NASB, NIV, NLT) and places the final he (ה) on the beginning of the next word as an interrogative particle. Topheth was a place near Jerusalem used as a burial ground (see Jer 7:32; 19:11).

The Hebrew text reads literally, “Also it is made ready for the king, one makes it deep and wide.” If one takes the final he (ה) on תָּפְתֶּה (tofteh) and prefixes it to גָּם (gam) as an interrogative particle (see the preceding note), one can translate, “Is it also made ready for the king?” In this case the question is rhetorical and expects an emphatic affirmative answer, “Of course it is!”
Apparently this alludes to some type of funeral rite. tn Heb “its pile of wood, fire and wood, one makes abundant.”

This is a study guide commentary, which

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This context refers to the many revolts against Assyria after the death of Sargon II in
705 B.C. These revolts by numerous vassal states were put down by
the new King Sennacherib.

- The Egyptian dynasty from which Hezekiah sought a political/military alliance was the Twenty-fifth
Dynasty. It was led by the Cushite/Nubian king, Shabaka, who aggressively tried to rally
all the small nations, from the head waters of the Euphrates to Egypt's borders, against Assyria.

- There are six woe oracles in this literary unit (i.e. Isa. 28-33).

- woe to the northern and southern tribes of Israel, Isa. 28

- woe to Jerusalem, Isa. 29:1-14

- woe to those who seek help in political alliances and not in YHWH, Isa. 29:15-24

- woe to those seeking help from Egypt, Isa. 30

- woe to those seeking help from Egypt, Isa. 31-32

- woe to Assyria, Isa. 33

NASB

"an unclean thing"

NRSV
"like filthy rags"

NJB
"like the polluted things"

Peshitta
"like unclean water of a menstrous woman"

This is the term (BDB 188) which denotes the rags used during a woman's menstrual
period (cf. Lev. 15:33; 20:18). This would have been a strong cultural idiom of a ceremonially unclean
thing which must be set apart (cf. Isa. 64:6).

The LXX (REB) takes the next word "be gone" (BDB 422, KB 425) as a similar term, "feces,"
which would be another cultural idiom of ceremonial defilement.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 30:23-26

23Then He will give you rain for the seed which you will sow in the ground, and
bread from the yield of the ground, and it will be rich and plenteous; on that day your livestock will graze in a roomy pasture.
24Also the oxen and the donkeys which work the ground will eat salted fodder, which has been winnowed with shovel and
fork. 25On every lofty mountain and on every high hill there will be streams running with water on the day of the great slaughter,
when the towers fall. 26The light of the moon will be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times
brighter, like the light of seven days, on the day the Lord binds up the fracture of His people and
heals the bruise He has inflicted.

30:23-26 This describes the agricultural and pastoral blessing promised to Abraham's seed if they
walk in YHWH's covenant (cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-28).

- rain at the proper time, Isa. 30:23,25, cf. Isa. 35:6,7; 41:18; 43:19,20

- good crops, Isa. 30:23

- rich (BDB 206)

- plenteous (BDB 1032)

- green pastures for the livestock, Isa. 30:23, cf. Isa. 32:20

- a special food for the working livestock, Isa. 30:24 (term BDB 330 is found only here)

- enemies defeated, Isa. 30:25 ("on every high hill." This same idiom was used for Ba'al
worship in Hosea)

- plenty of light for health and growth, Isa. 30:26, cf. Isa. 60:20-21 (seven being symbolic of the perfect
amount and light being symbolic of God's presence, i.e. His name, Isa. 30:27)

30:26 These blessings of restoration (cf. Isa. 11:6-9; Rom. 8:18-22; see full note at 30:20) are after

- the day of great slaughter when the towers fall, Isa. 30:25

- the day of the Lord binds up the fracture of His people, Isa. 30:26

- the day the Lord heals the bruise He has inflicted, Isa. 30:26

Notice #2 and #3 are imagery of YHWH as the great physician!

▣ "heals the bruise He has inflicted" This phrase and others like it (i.e. Deut. 32:39; 1 Sam. 2:6;
2 Kgs. 5:7; Job 5:18; Isa. 45:7; Jer. 1:10; 24:6; 31:28; Hosea 6:1; Amos 3:6) have caused moderns to question
the merciful character of God. These are all idiomatic ways of asserting monotheism (i.e. one and only
one causality; see full note at Isa. 14:24-27). Modern western people assume that there are many causalities in
their experiences and their histories. The Bible asserts the sovereignty of God in all areas of reality. He is
present and active!

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 30:27-33

27Behold, the name of the Lord comes from a remote place;

Burning is His anger and dense is His smoke;

His lips are filled with indignation

And His tongue is like a consuming fire;

28His breath is like an overflowing torrent,

Which reaches to the neck,

To shake the nations back and forth in a sieve,

And to put in the jaws of the peoples the bridle which leads to ruin.

29You will have songs as in the night when you keep the festival,

And gladness of heart as when one marches to the sound of the flute,

To go to the mountain of the Lord, to the Rock of Israel.

30And the Lord will cause His voice of authority to be heard,

And the descending of His arm to be seen in fierce anger,

And in the flame of a consuming fire

In cloudburst, downpour and hailstones.

31For at the voice of the Lord Assyria will be terrified,

When He strikes with the rod.

32And every blow of the rod of punishment,

Which the Lord will lay on him,

Will be with the music of tambourines and lyres;

And in battles, brandishing weapons, He will fight them.

33For Topheth has long been ready,

Indeed, it has been prepared for the king.

He has made it deep and large,

A pyre of fire with plenty of wood;

The breath of the Lord, like a torrent of brimstone, sets it afire.

30:27-33 This strophe reflects God's judgment on Assyria in the imagery of a theophany as an
approaching storm (cf. Exod. 19:16ff; Jdg. 5:4-5; Ps. 18:7ff; 50:3-5; Hab. 3:3-4).

- elements of theophany ‒ Isa. 30:27, 30a-c, 33e

- elements of storm ‒ Isa. 30:28, 30d

- elements of restoration ‒ Isa. 30:29

- elements of judgment ‒ Assyria, Isa. 30:31-33

30:27 "the name of the Lord comes. . ." The name represents the personal
presence of YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "Burning in His anger. . .lips. . .tongue" The only vocabulary humans have to descirbe God is

- analogy ‒ what He is like

- negation ‒ what He is not

- personification

YHWH is an eternal, spiritual Being present throughout the entire universe and not limited by
time/space. Humans must speak of Him in practical, but not exhaustive, terms.

The second term (משאה, BDB 673,

משאת, Isa. 30:38, denotes rising smoke from a
burning city. The context of Isa. 30:27 is one of theophany and judgment, so both fit.

- exaltation, denoting a cloud (i.e. Shekinah)

- heavy smoke

▣ "lips. . .tongue" This is imagery about the power of YHWH's revelation (cf. vv. 30a, 31a;
Isa. 11:4; 49:2; 55:11). This is parallel to "breath" (vv. 28, 33). YHWH's word equals YHWH's personal presence. To
ignore either is disastrous!

In the NT this same imagery is seen in Jesus with a two-edged sword coming out of His
mouth (cf. Rev. 1:16; 2:12; 19:21).

30:28 "Which reaches to the neck" This same idiom was used of the Assyrian invasion in Isa. 8:8.
Here, the idiom is reversed and YHWH fights on Judah's side against Assyria.

The MT has "to sift (lit. "swing" or "to move to and fro") nations with the
sieve (BDB 632) of worthlessness (BDB 996)." The interpretive question is, "Do we seek the
imagery from

- the VERB ‒ a sieve swinging back and forth to separate grain from the husk

- the NOUN ‒ nothingness, emptiness, vanity possibly denoting idol worship

In context, it is the mercenary army of the Assyrian Empire with its King that will be judged,
cf. vv. 30-33. Verses 23-26 and 29 refer to Judah being blessed.

30:29 "the mountain of the Lord, to the Rock of Israel" These are idioms
for the temple in Jerusalem because of parallelism. Often "the rock" refers to YHWH Himself (cf. Isa. 17:10;
Deut. 32:4,18,30; 1 Sam. 2:2; Ps. 18:2,31,46; 28:1; 31:3; 42:9).

30:30 "His voice" Literally, "the majesty (BDB 217) of His voice." God's will is accomplished through
speaking (i.e. creation, Genesis 1). His voice is effective (cf. Isa. 45:23; 55:11; Matt. 24:35). The
imagery of Jesus with a two-edged sword (cf. Heb. 4:12) coming out of His mouth (cf. Isa. 49:2;
Rev. 1:16; 2:12,16; 19:15) is theologically parallel, as is "the rod of His mouth" in Isa. 11:4.

▣ "hailstones" God used them in Jos. 10:11 as a way to defeat the Canaanites and give
victory to Israel (cf. Jos. 10:14,42; 23:3,10).

The VERB (BDB 369, KB 365, Qal IMPERFECT)
literally means "be shattered," denoting a complete defeat in battle which is preceded by a numbing,
paralyzing fear of the upcoming defeat (cf. Isa. 7:8; 8:9 [thrice]; 9:4; 20:5; 30:31; 31:4,9; 37:27; 51:6,7). YHWH
is fighting on His people's side against Assyria. The fear and panic and loss experienced by Israel and
Judah is now being felt by Assyria, which in the past, was the rod of YHWH's anger (cf. Isa. 10:5).

▣ "He strikes with a rod" In Isaiah 10:5, Assyria is called the "rod of God's anger," but
here the roles are reversed and God is back on His people's side. The rod (BDB 986) now feels the rod!

30:32 The judgment of the Lord is expressed by the imagery of a
beating with a rod. It is possible that the next two lines (Isa. 30:32c,d) depict

- strokes being given at the musical beat of rejoicing

- that Judah's rejoicing follows Assyria's defeat by YHWH (cf. Isa. 30:32d).

30:33 "Topheth" This Hebrew word, found only here, apparently means a "place of burning" (BDB 1075).
It is often identified with "Topheth" (BDB 1075 II), which was a valley outside the southern walls of
Jerusalem and is often used in connection with the worship of the god, Molech (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH). Here,
the context could imply

- a place of sacrifice to YHWH prepared by the king of His restored people

- the funeral pyre for Assyria's king prepared by YHWH Himself (cf. Isa. 31:9)

- "the King" which refers to Molech, the Phoenician fire god (cf. Lev. 18:21)

In context #2 fits best.
